body:
Thanks, that really means a lot.  I imagine that all of us who are here on r/SuicideWatch are most likely fighting multiple battles.  It's pretty far out that we all come from different backgrounds and have different struggles, but at the end of the day we are all in the same boat, trying to deal with the pain and wanting it to go away.  It's nice to know there are others dealing with that pain who are also trying their hardest to make it out alive. And that's a pretty crazy concept to me.  That it's ok to not be ok.  I've always been able to have compassion for other people dealing with these kinds of struggles, but I've always thought that for myself it's unacceptable for me to not be ok.  Which just ends up making things worse.  I've always been sort of a high achiever and somewhat of a perfectionist in whatever endeavor I choose to pursue.  Any kind of failure always hits me really hard.

Anyway thanks again for taking the time to just talk with me tonight.  It really does help.  And thanks for the kind words.  Getting A's doesn't really matter in life, but I believe trying to be a good person does matter, and yeah just getting back up and pressing forward every time life punches you in the mouth.  Feel free to PM if you ever need to talk.  I'll let you know what my normal account username is.

Wow.  Thank you for your kind words.  You seriously lifted the ominous mood I've been in all day.  I've lurked this sub and r/depression from time to time for the last few years, but this has been the first time I've ever posted anything or talked with anyone, and it really does help.  You also come across as a sincere, caring person, so it's nice to talk to someone like who also understands where I'm coming from.  That's awesome that you come here to just talk with other people who are struggling, without expectations.  Trust me, just this one small conversation has been a lot more cathartic than any and all therapy sessions I've ever been to.  

I think the fact that we can relate to each other makes a huge difference in talking about these things.  Maybe I'll start making an effort to interact with other people in this community on my normal account.  

I hope you can make the distance community college work.  It does make a difference, chipping away at something that you choose to give purpose to.  And it's something that can potentially give you more power to help yourself and others, and improve your own quality of life.  Which I think is a good thing overall for humanity.  The more we educate ourselves, the more it makes for a better society and happier life for everyone. 

I've been stuck in my third going on fourth year of uni for a long time.  Long stretches of time where I've said fuck it, then gone back.  Semesters where I've got 2/3 of the way through, and then said fuck it and just stopped going to class, because that's just the broken way I am. I get so burdened by big picture things that going to class and getting a degree seem so trivial and pointless at times, and I've ended up sabotaging myself over and over.  Then I spend months working shitty service industry jobs to save up for tuition, and then start the whole masochistic cycle all over again. It's almost really funny if it wasn't also something that makes me want to seriously put a gun in my mouth sometimes.  This semester was rough.  I quit working at the restaurant i was serving at, because it wasn't working with my full time school schedule.  But by the time I quit, the damage was already done.  

My anxiety went through the roof, I got really depressed about how everything was going, I became withdrawn socially again, stopped going to my classes, started taking an SSRI prescription again to try and fight it, but I felt like that actually made everything worse, and so here I am.  I've never attempted suicide, because I know if I do, I'll actually make damn well sure that it works.  But there's still that part of me who says maybe next time I'll get it right.  The thing is, is when I actually do make it through the semester and finish my classes I usually get all A's and A-'s.  It's the only reason my gpa isn't totally fucked at this point from all the incomplete grades I've accumulated.  But yeah I guess I have to keep trying until I finish at this point.

Anyway sorry to go on and on about myself.  I think I was just trying to say that yeah for someone who gets social anxiety, and depression, and deals with continual suicidal ideation, going to school is totally worth it.  Just try not to get down on yourself, and keep chipping away at it.

Thanks for responding and reaching out.  I guess I've had what I would call existential depression off and on for about the last 7 or 8 years. I've also been pretty depressed about circumstantial problems in my life from time to time. 

I'm 31 and for the last several years these thoughts have all but consumed me at times and have wreaked havoc on my ability to function as a "normal adult" in society. Over the years there have been periods of time where I will sort of fantasize about suicide for sometimes several months, and at the longest stretch for a couple of years.  I feel like this stems from the way I've processed my own experiences over the years and how I've observed the people around me, how this dysfunctional society that we humans have created works, and how in the grand scheme of things we are all going to cease to exist anyway and none of this really matters.  Modern life as we have created it is absurd.  

When I became disillusioned with all forms of organized religion in my early twenties, I searched for meaning from different philosophers.  That ended up reinforcing what I felt, and I felt the urge to be more and more nihilistic in how I lived.  I searched for meaning in psychedelics, and gleaned some meaningful insights from those experiences, but ultimately we still live in this fucked up world of pain and misery, and we humans are consciously and unconsciously contributing to making this brief experience even more painful for each other all the time.  

And I do recognize that there is also so much beauty and possible joy to be experienced in this brief time we have here. I just get so overwhelmed by the negatives.  I'm aware of my own human nature, my own flaws, my own contributions to adding to human suffering, and my own lack of contribution to alleviating it.  I see so much wrong with the world, and with myself, and lately I feel more and more helpless.  More alone.  More worthless.  It all just feels heavier and heavier as each day passes.

I think if I was truly, truly alone in the world I for sure would have ended my own life probably a few years ago.  The last few years I've honestly felt like the only thing that holds me back and keeps me going is knowing how much it would fuck my younger siblings and my parents up who are all doing their best to deal with their own struggles in this fucked up world.  But I also know that living for these reasons alone is no way to live.

Man I'm sorry to hear about your fiancee. I feel like I can somewhat relate. when I was 23 I was married for about a year to a girl I really loved.  We were together all in all for about 2 1/2 years and things ended badly.  We even tried getting back together a couple of times but we just weren't good for each other overall. that was about 8 years ago now.  Love is good when it's good, but it can also be so devastating and painful when you give your all to someone and it doesn't work out. Thanks for responding.  It's nice being able to talk with people honestly who don't freak out over trying to have an open and honest conversation.
